en: class for advanced learners; the highest-level class

examples.en: Next semester I'll study in the advanced class.
The advanced class has a lot of discussion.
I did well on the test and moved up to the advanced class.

examples.ko: 고급반에 들어가려면 레벨 테스트를 봐야 해요.
examples.en: To get into the advanced class, you have to take a level test.
The friends in the advanced class speak Korean really well.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 고급반이 아니라서 신문 기사가 어려워요.
examples.en: I'm not in the advanced class yet, so news articles are hard for me.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '초급반', '중급반'이에요. 학원이나 어학당 수업을 말할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: I passed the test and moved up to the advanced class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 단계 높은 반으로 옮길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving up to a higher class.
phrases.en_equiv: to move up to the advanced class

phrases.en: I'm studying in the intermediate class now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고급반 바로 아래 단계의 반이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The class level right below 고급반.

phrases.en: The advanced class is hard but fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업 내용이나 분위기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about the lessons or atmosphere.

explain_en: Its companions are '초급반' (beginner class) and '중급반' (intermediate class). It is often used for classes at academies and language institutes.

examples.en: When you reach the upper grades of elementary school, the homework increases.
The older girls from the upper grades helped us.
This book is for the upper grades.
The lower grades and the upper grades have different break times.
My younger sibling will soon move up to the upper grades.
It is a slightly difficult problem for the upper grades.

explain: 반대말은 '저학년'이에요. 초등학교에서는 보통 1~2학년을 저학년, 3~4학년을 중학년, 5~6학년을 고학년이라고 불러요. 한 학년이 아니라 여러 학년을 묶어서 가리키는 말이에요.

phrases.en: Upper-grade students have longer classes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '학생'을 붙여 그 학년의 사람들을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 학생 refers to the students in those grades.

phrases.en: The lower grades and upper grades play together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '저학년'과 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used together with its opposite, 저학년.

phrases.en: My child is in the upper grades now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 아이나 학생이 몇 학년쯤인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say roughly which grades a child is in.

explain_en: The opposite is 저학년 (lower grades). In elementary school, grades 1-2 are usually 저학년, grades 3-4 are 중학년 and grades 5-6 are 고학년. It groups several grades together rather than naming a single one.

examples.en: My friend's handwriting style is really pretty.

examples.ko: 이 글씨체가 읽기 편해서 계속 써요.
examples.en: I keep using this lettering style because it is easy to read.
I looked at my teacher's handwriting and copied it.
The mood changes depending on the lettering style.

examples.ko: 손으로 쓴 것 같은 글씨체로 카드를 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: I decorated the card in a hand-written looking style.

examples.ko: 글씨체까지 닮은 두 사람이 쌍둥이 같아요.
examples.en: The two people look like twins, even down to their handwriting.

explain: '글씨가 예뻐요'는 쓴 솜씨를 칭찬하는 말이고, '글씨체가 예뻐요'는 글자 모양의 스타일을 말해요. 컴퓨터에서는 '글꼴'이나 '폰트'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I changed the font of my presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터에서 쓰는 글자 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to a font on a computer.

phrases.en: I changed my handwriting style to look nicer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 모양을 다르게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when changing the letter style.

phrases.en: The two people's handwriting is different.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글자 모양을 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to compare letter styles.

explain_en: '글씨가 예뻐요' praises how well someone writes, while '글씨체가 예뻐요' talks about the style of the letter shapes. On a computer people say '글꼴' or '폰트'.

en: (couple) to work together; to work for a double income; to work in double harness

examples.ko: 저와 아내는 둘 다 일하니까 맞벌이해요.
examples.en: My wife and I both work, so we are a two-income couple.

examples.ko: 부모님은 오래 맞벌이하셔서 저를 할머니가 키워 주셨어요.
examples.en: My parents both worked for a long time, so my grandmother raised me.
I want us both to keep working even after the baby is born.
Couples who both work share the housework.

examples.ko: 예전에는 맞벌이했지만 지금은 아내가 쉬고 있어요.
examples.en: We both worked before, but now my wife is taking a break.
Housing is expensive, so we have no choice but to both work.

explain: '맞벌이 부부'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요. 반대는 한 사람만 돈을 버는 '외벌이'예요. 주어는 부부나 가족이어서 한 사람이 혼자 '맞벌이해요'라고 하면 어색해요.

phrases.en: Dual-income couples are busy every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사처럼 '부부' 앞에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used before '부부' like a noun.

phrases.en: We both work, so we don't have much time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유를 말할 때 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to give a reason.

phrases.en: My parents don't both work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람만 돈을 벌 때 쓰는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for when only one person earns.
phrases.en_equiv: not to have a double income

explain_en: It also works as a noun, as in '맞벌이 부부'. The opposite is '외벌이', where only one person earns money. The subject is a couple or a family, so one person alone saying '맞벌이해요' sounds odd.

examples.ko: 수업 진도가 너무 빨라서 따라가기 힘들어요.
examples.en: The class is moving so fast that it's hard to keep up.
Today we covered the textbook up to page 50.
Teacher, how far have we gotten?
Because of the exam, we rushed to finish the material.

examples.ko: 저는 혼자 공부해서 진도를 마음대로 정해요.
examples.en: I study alone, so I set my own pace.
I was absent and missed the lesson material.

explain: 진도는 수업이나 공부가 어디까지 나아갔는지를 말해요. '진도를 나가다', '진도가 빠르다/느리다'처럼 써요. 일이 얼마나 되었는지는 '진행 상황'이라고 하고, 진도는 주로 공부나 수업에 써요.

phrases.en: This class moves quickly through the material.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이 빨리 나아갈 때 '진도'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 진도 when a class moves ahead quickly.

phrases.en: I review so that I can keep up with the lessons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이 나아가는 속도에 맞춰 공부한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means studying at the same pace as the class.
phrases.en_equiv: to keep up with the lessons

phrases.en: Because I was sick, my study progress became slow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공부가 천천히 나아갈 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when studying moves ahead slowly.

explain_en: 진도 is how far a class or study has progressed. It is used as '진도를 나가다' or '진도가 빠르다/느리다'. How far work has gone is '진행 상황'; 진도 is mainly for study and lessons.

en: to enter a higher education institution

examples.en: I'm entering university next year.
My older sister went on to graduate school.
I'm going to enter a school to study art.

examples.ko: 고등학교를 졸업하고 바로 진학하는 학생이 많아요.
examples.en: Many students go straight on to higher education after high school.

examples.ko: 성적이 좋으면 원하는 학교에 진학하기 쉬워요.
examples.en: With good grades, it's easier to get into the school you want.
After entering the school, I lived in a dorm.

explain: 진학하다는 지금 학교를 마치고 더 높은 단계의 학교로 가는 거예요. '입학'은 학교에 들어가는 일 자체이고, 진학은 다음 단계로 올라간다는 점이 달라요. 보통 '대학교에 진학하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 써요.

phrases.en: I want to go on to university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로의 학교 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about future school plans.
phrases.en_equiv: I want to go on to school

phrases.en: My younger sibling entered high school this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중학교를 마치고 다음 학교로 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when moving on after middle school.

phrases.en: I had a school-choice consultation with my teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어느 학교로 갈지 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when discussing which school to go to.

explain_en: 진학하다 is to finish one school and move up to the next level. Unlike '입학' (entering a school), it stresses stepping up to the next stage. It takes the particle 에: '대학교에 진학하다'.

en: to vote; to cast a ballot

examples.en: On election day I vote at the school.
Our class voted for a favorite song.
I will vote for the first time this time.
The number of people who vote keeps growing.
Opinions differed, so we voted and decided.
We voted with friends and chose a restaurant.

explain: 선거뿐 아니라 친구들끼리 메뉴를 고를 때도 '투표하다'를 가볍게 써요. 누구를 뽑는지 말하려면 '~에게 투표하다'라고 해요. 투표하러 가는 곳은 '투표소'예요.

phrases.en: I'm going to vote tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선거날에 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used around election day.

phrases.en: I voted for Minsu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누구를 뽑았는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say who you voted for.

phrases.en: We decide the lunch menu by voting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍게 무엇을 고를 때도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used lightly for casual choices.

explain_en: It is not only for elections; friends also use it lightly when choosing a menu. To say who you vote for, use the pattern 'vote for someone'. The place you go to vote is the polling station.
